note: current_text is the running head συνστενάζω plus the end of the previous entry (συνστέλλω, 'ing-sheet, or possibly, I lay out, Ac. v 6; (b) I contract, compress; hence I shorten, 1 Cor. vii 29.') continued from p. 258, not συστενάζω; the real συνστενάζω entry is entry 5042

text: συνστενάζω, I groan together.
συνστοιχέω (properly a military term, I keep in line or file), I correspond exactly to.
συνστρατιώτης, a fellow-soldier, comrade in arms.
σύνσωμος, sharing in a body: it has been taken as fellow-slave (see σῶμα).
συντάσσω, I direct, instruct, command.
συντέμνω, I cut down; hence I contract, limit, restrict the scope of.
συντηρέω, I keep safe.
συντίθημι, mid. and pass. I make a compact (agreement) with (together), I covenant with, I agree.
συντόμως, briefly.
συντρέχω, I run (rush) together, lit. or met.
συντρίβω, (a) I break; I bruise; (b) I trample upon, crush, Rom. xvi 20: I maul, Lk. ix 39; (c) met. pass. I am stunned, crushed, [Lk.] iv 18.
σύντριμμα, destruction, ruin.
σύντροφος, foster-brother: such is the lit. rendering, but it would appear to be a court title, and might therefore be translated a courtier.
συντυγχάνω, I encounter, come up with, come close to.
gloss: I encounter, come up with, come close to

text: Συντύχη, Syntyche, a woman member of the church at Philippi.
gloss: Syntyche, a woman member of the church at Philippi

text: συνυποκρίνομαι, pass. I dissemble along with.
συνυπουργέω, I co-operate in a subordinate capacity.
gloss: I co-operate in a subordinate capacity

text: συνχέω (cf. συνχύννω), I confound.
συνχράομαι, I have intercourse with, I associate with.
gloss: I have intercourse with, I associate with

text: συνωδίνω, I unite in suffering travail (birth pangs, severe pain).
gloss: I unite in suffering travail (birth pangs, severe pain)

text: συνωμοσία, a conspiracy, plot.
Συράκουσαι (plur. because originally, as in many similar cases, both a citadel and a settlement in the valley), Syracuse, in E. Sicily.
Συρία, Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia.
gloss: Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia

text: Σύρος, Syrian, belonging to Syria.
Συροφοινίκισσα, Syro-phoenician, i. e. Phoenician (of Syria, in contrast to Carthage and its territory in N. Africa).
Σύρτις, Syrtis, a quicksand off the coast of N. Africa.
gloss: Syrtis, a quicksand off the coast of N. Africa

text: σύρω, I drag, pull, draw.
συσπαράσσω, I throw violently on the ground.
gloss: I throw violently on the ground

text: σύσσημον, a signal agreed upon between two parties.
gloss: a signal agreed upon between two parties

text: συστατικός, recommending, introducing.
συστρέφω, (a) tr. I gather together, collect, Ac. xxviii 3; (b) mid. either, I press together (about one) or I stroll.
συστροφή, a crowding together; hence, a seditious meeting, Ac. xix 40; a conspiracy, Ac. xxiii 12.
Συχάρ, Sychar, a ‘city’ of Samaria.
Συχέμ, Sychem, Shechem, Sicyma (later Neapolis, from which modern Nablus), a city of Samaria.
σφαγή, slaughter, sacrifice (of an animal); πρόβατον σφαγῆς (Hebraism), a sheep destined for sacrifice.
σφάγιον, a sacrifice (of an animal).
σφοδρῶς, exceedingly.
σφυδρόν, an ankle-bone.
σχῆμα, the outward (changeable) fashion (form).
σχίσμα, a cleavage, cleft, split, rent: so met. a division in a crowd, due to difference of opinion, a party division.
σχοινίον, a rope; a cable, hawser.
σχολάζω, (a) I have leisure, c. dat. for, 1 Cor. vii 5; (b) I stand empty, of a house, Mt. xii 44, [Lk.] xi 25.
σχολή, a school, or lecture-hall.
σωματικός, (a) bodily, hence almost = visible, tangible, Lk. iii 22; (b) bodily, physical, contrasted with ‘mental’, ‘spiritual’, 1 Tim. iv 8.
σωματικῶς, bodily, in a bodily way, almost = visibly.
Σώπατρος (a pet-form of Σωσίπατρος), Sopater, son of Pyrrhus, and a Christian of Beroea in Macedonia.
σωρεύω, I heap: c. acc. et dat., I overwhelm some one with something, 2 Tim. iii 6.
Σωσθένης, Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue at Corinth (Ac. xviii 17), probably to be identified with the Christian of 1 Cor. i 1.
gloss: Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue at Corinth

text: Σωσίπατρος, Sosipater, a Christian at Rome.
σωτήριος, bringing salvation, fraught with salvation.
σωφρονίζω, (lit. I make σώφρων, hence) I admonish, warn.
σωφρονισμός, self-discipline.
σωφρόνως, sobermindedly.
σωφροσύνη, sound sense, sobermindedness.
σώφρων (from σῶς, safe, sound, and φρήν, the mind), soberminded, prudent.
Ταβειθά, Tabitha, a Christian woman at Joppa.
gloss: Tabitha, a Christian woman at Joppa

text: τάγμα (a military term), rank; division.
τακτός, appointed, arranged.
ταλαιπωρέω, I am wretched (afflicted, in distress).
ταλαιπωρία, wretchedness, distress, misery.
ταλαίπωρος, wretched, miserable.
ταλαντιαῖος, a talent in weight or size. (But ἀγῶνες ταλαντιαῖοι are games where the value of the prizes amounted to a talent.)
gloss: a talent in weight or size

text: ταλειθά (Aramaic), maiden.
ταμεῖον (syncopated from ταμιεῖον, and first appearing in syncopated form in first cent. after Christ), an office, a private room: also a store, Lk. xii 24 (being derived from ταμίας, ‘a steward’).
ταπεινός, of low estate, poor (and thus despised by the mass of mankind); also poor in spirit, meek, a notion often combined by the Jews with the previous.
ταπεινόφρων, meek-minded; humble-minded.
ταπείνωσις, a being brought low, Ac. viii 33, James i 10: meekness; humility (ταπείνωσις et humilitas uirtutis dicitur et humilitas adflictionis, Ambrose, expos. ps. cxviii 20 10 § 2).
τάραχος, disturbance.
Ταρσεύς, belonging to Tarsus, a Tarsian.
Ταρσός, Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia.
gloss: Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia

text: ταρταρόω, I send to Tartarus (Tartarus being in the Greek view a place of punishment under the earth, to which, for example, the Titans were sent).
ταῦρος, a bull; an ox.
ταφή (sepultura), burial.
τάφος, a tomb; sepulchral monument.
τάχα, perhaps.
ταχινός, speedy, possibly sudden.
τάχειον, see ταχέως.
note: Target points to the entry τάχιστα ('τάχιστα, see ταχέως.') at the top of p. 265, which is the superlative, not τάχιον; the entry for τάχιον is Souter's τάχειον at the foot of p. 264 ('τάχειον, see ταχέως.'), given here as text

text: τάχος, quickness; ἐν τάχει, adverbially, speedily, quickly.
ταχύς, quick.
τεῖχος, a wall, especially the wall of a city.
τεκμήριον, an infallible proof, a piece of certain (convincing) evidence.
τεκνίον (a diminutive form, suggesting affection, applied to grown up persons), little child.
τεκνογονεῖν, to bear a child (children), to become a mother.
gloss: to bear a child (children), to become a mother

text: τεκνογονία, child-bearing; motherhood.
τεκνοτροφέω, I bring up children.
τέκτων, a worker in wood, a carpenter.
gloss: a worker in wood, a carpenter

text: τελειότης, moral completeness (perfection).
τελείως, perfectly, absolutely, with νήφοντες, 1 Pet. i 13.
τελείωσις, a bringing to completion (perfection, fulfilment).
τελειωτής, a completer, perfecter.
τελεσφορέω, I bring (the fruit) to maturity.
τελευτή (lit. end), death.
τελώνιον, a revenue office; a custom-house.
Τέρτιος (Latin), Tertius, a Roman (?) Christian, who wrote the Epistle to the Romans at Paul’s dictation.
Τέρτυλλος (Latin), Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of St. Paul at Caesarea.
gloss: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor

text: τεσσαρακονταετής, of forty years, forty years long.
gloss: of forty years, forty years long

text: τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος, fourteenth.
τεταρταῖος, of the fourth day (Greek idiom often personalises such adjectives), four days since he died.
τετρααρχέω, I rule as tetrarch.
τετραάρχης, a tetrarch, that is, the ruler of a fourth part of a territory divided into four parts for efficient government, a division sometimes found in the Roman East.
τετράγωνος, with four corners, square.
τετράδιον (quaternio), a quaternion, a group of four soldiers.
gloss: a quaternion, a group of four soldiers

text: τετρακόσιοι, four hundred.
τετράμηνος, adj., of four months (understand χρόνος): hence, four months.
τετραπλόος (quadruplex, quadruplus), fourfold, four times as much.
τετράπους (quadrupes), four-footed; a quadruped.
τεφρόω, I cover with, or I convert into, ashes.
gloss: I cover with, or I convert into, ashes

text: τέχνη, art, handicraft, trade.
τεχνίτης, a craftsman, an artisan: c. gen. a designer, Heb. xi 10.
τήκομαι, I melt (intr.).
τηλαυγῶς (so old MSS. [including W, the Washington (Freer) Gospels], clearly from afar, clearly: but others of equal age read δηλαυγῶς, which see).
τηλικοῦτος, so large, so great.
τήρησις, (a) a keeping, an observance, 1 Cor. vii 19; (b) a place of custody.
Τιβεριάς, Tiberias, a town in Galilee on the western border of the sea called after it.
Τιβέριος, Tiberius, the second Roman emperor (died A.D. 37).
τιμιότης, preciousness.
Τίμων, Timon, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem.
gloss: Timon, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem

text: τιμωρέω, I punish.
τιμωρία, (deserved) punishment.
τίνω, I pay.
τίτλος (Latin) (titulus), an inscription.
τοιγαροῦν, accordingly, wherefore.
τοίνυν, so.
τοιόσδε, of such character, to the following effect.
gloss: of such character, to the following effect

text: τοῖχος, a wall.
τόκος (from τίκτω, cf. Shakespeare’s ‘breed of barren metal’), interest.
τολμηρῶς, courageously.
note: Souter's headword is the positive adverb τολμηρῶς; no separate entry for the comparative τολμηρότερον

text: τολμητής, a shameless and headstrong man.
τομός, cutting, with cutting power.
note: Souter's headword is the positive τομός; no separate entry for the comparative τομώτερος

text: τόξον, a bow (and arrows).
τοπάζιον, a topaz.
τοὐναντίον (syncopated from τὸ ἐναντίον, the opposite), as adv. on the contrary.
τοὔνομα (syncopated from τὸ ὄνομα), as adv., by name.
τράγος, a goat.
τραπεζίτης (from τράπεζα, money-changer’s table), a money-changer, a banker.
τραῦμα, a wound.
τραυματίζω, I wound.

τραχηλίζω (from τράχηλος, ‘neck’, probably referring originally to the bending back of the head in sacrifice so as to expose the neck: but, whatever be the origin of the expression, the met. sense is clear): τετραχηλισμένα, open, manifest.
τράχηλος, the neck: τὸν ἑαυτῶν τράχηλον ὑποθεῖναι, to lay down their own necks, i. e. to risk their own lives.
τραχύς, rough.
Τραχωνιτίς, Trachonitic, belonging to Trachon, adj. applied to a hilly region (inhabited by a nomad tribe), considerably to the south of Damascus, called also Ituraean.
τρέμω, I tremble.
τρέφω, I nourish, feed; I bring up, Lk. iv 16: met., James v 5.
τρῆμα, opening, hole; eye of needle (perhaps a favourite term of medical writers).
τριακόσιοι, three hundred.
τρίβολος, a thistle.
τρίβος, a path, track.
τριετία, a period of three years, three years.
gloss: a period of three years, three years

text: τρίζω, I grind, crunch.
τρίμηνος, lasting three months: acc. neut. as adv. three months.
note: Souter's headword is the adjective τρίμηνος; the NT form τρίμηνον is covered by 'acc. neut. as adv. three months'

text: τρίστεγος, having three roofs, with three floors (stories): hence neut. as noun, the third floor, but it is uncertain whether the ground floor was counted or not in this enumeration; if so, we should have to translate, the second floor.
gloss: having three roofs, with three floors (stories)
note: Souter's headword is the adjective τρίστεγος; the NT form τρίστεγον is covered by 'hence neut. as noun, the third floor'

text: τρισχίλιοι, three thousand.
τρίτον, acc. neut. of adj., generally with definite article, as adv., the third time; third, in the third place, 1 Cor. xii 28.
τρίχινος, made of hair.
τρόμος, trembling.
τροπή, any change undergone by any object; hence referring to night and day, or the waxing and waning of the moon, the solstice, &c.
gloss: any change undergone by any object

text: τροποφορέω, I bear (endure) the ways (disposition) of (v. l.).
Τρόφιμος, Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia.
gloss: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia
